prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1423; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured reports the other vehicle backed into the driver's side rear quarter panel. Both drivers exited their vehicles and exchanged information. Police were not called. Photos of both vehicles requested from insured.

Entry 2: Claimant's attorney's office contacted this adjuster and advised that all communication regarding the claimant should be directed to counsel going forward. Claimant reports neck and back strain from the impact. Medical authorization requested through counsel. No direct contact with the claimant to occur.

Entry 3: Received photographs of the insured vehicle showing scuffing and a cracked taillight lens on the driver's side. Estimate for repairs requested from the preferred shop. Liability appears probable against the other driver based on the insured's account and the position of the vehicles as photographed. Witness statement not yet obtained.

Entry 4: Counsel forwarded initial treatment records indicating evaluation for cervical and lumbar strain and a recommended course of physical therapy. Records reviewed and placed in the injury file. Requested complete records from the prior two years to assess pre-existing complaints. Follow-up with counsel scheduled.

Entry 5: Spoke with defense counsel regarding the claim status. Liability position under review pending receipt of the complete medical file and the repair estimate. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the reported injury. File flagged for supervisor review at the next claims meeting.
